title: TransCUPtomics autoencoder predicts tissue of origin in cancers of unknown primary
summary: A variational autoencoder trained on 20,918 samples (94 categories) predicted tissue of origin from RNA-seq with 96% accuracy on reference data. The origin was identified in 38 of 48 CUP patients (79%), and eight of 11 prospective patients (73%) received first-line therapy guided by the prediction, with responses in most. The clinical cohorts are small.
ai_technology: Variational autoencoder classifier on RNA-sequencing data
organization: INSERM; Université Paris Sciences et Lettres; La Ligue Contre le Cancer

evidence.tested: Application to 37 retrospective and 11 prospective CUP patients.
evidence.unknown: Responses are not causal proof of benefit; cohort size is small. Abstract-based; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A variational autoencoder predicted tissue of origin and supported interpretation by linking predictions to fusions and variants.
